Content: Young people are learning how to steward a long arc beyond 2224..

Classroom sizes are never too big or too small but just right for the people there, access to great teachers that meet students where they are at and have the resources they need to do so, teachers focus on understanding each student and how students are able to learn/hear the lessons, dismantling tradition views of white colonial schools, not teaching but storytelling, putting the whole person first and not mandated by a test in spring, no test decides worth, lifelong learning is the driver, including the 7 teachings
The education system follows the rhythm and flow of the seasons, and teaches lessons according to each.
Classrooms as laboratories for humanity. Each child as teacher and student.

Education is for the whole being- spirit included and tells the stories of all the ancestors of all the people, our struggles, centers peace making, generative conflict and conflict transformation, and 'ethnic studies' as well as traditional subjects

High quality education - kindergarten to college - is free and available to all. There is a variety of school curriculum that is modified to various learning styles and uses language and culture that is rooted in local community.

Learning has changed. The way we learn - nature teaches us, elders teach us, emotions teach us, art is valued, we help each other with community and conflict. We don't just leave two people on their own when they're having conflict.

Dismantling schools, intergenerational mentorship; what children are learning is being applied to the betterment of the collective; holistic medicine instead of synthetic drugs, community gardens and a bartering systems; peoples talents and offerings supercede money; equal sharing of resources for all, equality with resources; green energy; restorative practices to solve problems, violence is no longer tolerated; all creation has equal value and treated as such; children are treated as beloved; we go to our eldest ancestors to guide us
Children are learning to be engaged in the world rather than to be trained for a job. History is taught to not repeat our past but to understand where we came from.
Library has become a huge palace, and is a community center that provides so many things.

Science teachers art includes indigenizing lessons - the practice of teaching many ways of knowing, honoring cherished knowledge from Native peoples to a place, and also allow for the wisdom that comes anew by paying close attention and listening well.
Learning centers have developed to be intergenerational. They are a reflection of the fabric of society.
Education centers aren't just about employment - but fueling creativity and problem solving.
Young people are integrated into everyday life so they can learn experientially what is useful for them and the world. Their ideas are welcome and make a difference in the world now.
Teaching supports childhood. Play, exploration, challenge, purpose, collaboration, cause and effect learning, and shared responsibility. Families know their child's teacher and vice versa.
Education comes in many styles and disciplines, through multiple systems, with many ways of knowing.

Education and learning is well-rounded and blends indoor and outdoor environments (where/when possible; seasonally). Standards for what is learned are connected to each place and relevant to the community.
Mentorship/apprenticeship are highly sought after forms of education. You see children walking to older people's homes to begin the days work.
We greet each other in our languages.
Education would be lifelong, always based on teaching collective good, caring, sharing, and rooted in diversity being good for all of us.
There are rich learning portals into history, languages, ethnobotany, geography, health, etc.

Metacognition (thinking about thinking with conscious awareness) is valued and self-assessment is taught at all ages and with the very young. How am I doing? What do I understand and what do I need to ask more questions about? Memorization is a means to an end to be able to apply knowledge toward purpose. Education is valued and nurtured in many forms. Children, adults, and elders alike are free to follow their curiosity and learn with the support of mentors. Learning occurs through experiences, apprenticeship and relationships; there is no single or uniform path or curriculum meant to address massives. How silly that children used to be sorted together by age! Apprenticeships and mentorships are treasured. Young people are honored for their imagination and particular ability to love and feel in real time. Their stories are well considered and discussed. School time is for collaboration. Schools - places of learning - are where new ideas are encountered and new skills applied and honed. Skills work is connected to family practice/time at home which is supported and celebrated.
Free education based on following passion or talent, not what gets the best income.
Higher education is primarily online, doesn't cost anything and more people with various background are creating a more collective and holistic workforce.
Learning is collaborative, enthusiastically shared with others to deepen our communities skills.

Holistic. A collection of experiences not degrees. A range of disciplines and topics with a decentralization of power and co-creation with all campus partners. People and experiences over policy and procedures. Education is fee. Needs are met for all on campus. Community is created in many ways.
More online accessibility for education. Life-long education with continual change understanding ahd knowing that we can not contain knowledge and knowledge cannot be taken away.
Education is representative of the global majority, socio-economic origin, abd different life experiences.
Trade and skill development are valued.
Resource used in proactive measures, not from crisis.
Shared power, reduction of hierarchy.
We learn from students, co-education and reversal of hierarchy.
Free 99.
Erased boundaries, less limites, drop barriers.
Education is relevant not only to a person’s interests but also abilities.
Transfer of knowledge between generations. Learning from folks of all ages and identities.
People study fields of education because they love it, not because of money or prestige.
Students involved in higher education through co-creation. More folks from a wide array of backgrounds have a voice in decisions.
Can easily get to resources you need.

Education is an ecosystem where everything has a purpose ad every stage, variety of types/skills/contributions are essential. Needs vs. offerings compliment each other. Adaptations happen organically and are welcome.
Free parking on educational campuses. No fees for educational learning.
Culture of care on educational settings. Open conversations, healthy conflict. We can all learn from one another and value that learning.

Knowledge shared as a community not as a transaction. Creativity and curiosity fostered and embraced. Learning happens all around us, sitting outside sharing concepts, holistically connecting to all others.
Supports for parents and caregivers in educational settings
Sounds of music, laughter, joy and interconnectivity. This is (y)our place, this is (y)our community.
Array of Indigenous practices interwoven with policy, procedure, classroom activities/events/programs and environments.
De-centralized education, learning happens everywhere and is recognized as such. Student teacher dissolved and reimagined - mentors.
Access to abundance of resources, resource cycle is the norm.
Indigenous community leaders at the forefront of high educational ecosystems, a connected experience.
Storytelling and experiential learning are occurring everywhere.
No one questions if they belong or if there will be seven generations.
Educational ecosystems are influences with all learning. History is studied to learn how we move forward.

Government added universal but adaptable curriculum that helps kids navigate relationships of all sorts. The whole spectrum from romantic relationships to friendships, etc. The priority is for everyone to be able to talk to people from different faiths, races, cultures, etc. From young ages to old.
Children say, “Wow…those are teachers. I want to teach.” Teachers are revered and cared for so they can cultivate, share wisdom, bring out the best in people.
Their aren’t “rulers.” There are different kinds of teachers that help people learn how to be with each other.
We teach in an effort to show the infinitude of possibility – regardless of melanination or lack of melanination, crotch description, etc.
Knowledge transfer happens through letters we write to our children. We tell truths for them to read in their time. Truths of our humanity, healing, connection, fears.
We learn and share knowledge not through 140 characters or Tik Tok - knowledge transfer is slow, intentional, from an Elder.
We develop our babies by looking for their gifts - cultivating their senses and ability to feel and perceive.
Learning communities are shaped by Montessori principles - and learning is a lifelong endeavor.
Children are praised and celebrated for their curiosity, wonderment, imagination - instead of convenience and ‘’maturity’’
People travel in good ways to learn and experience with other communities.
Learning is understood to be important across the life cycle, and it’s understood that connecting across generations supports learning for all generations.
Learning is applied, and anything that requires memorization takes place in the context of putting that information to use.

Education happens everywhere. Kids curiosity happens everywhere–fields, shops, etc. They always feel comfortable asking what are you doing? How can I learn to do that? People enjoy answering the questions. Children are always welcome.
When an adult needs more time, they say “you can watch…and then…”
Active engagement of children means sitting with them, talking with them, listening. It’s known as place finding–which used to be called education.
Education, knowledge and reckoning with the past are at the forefront of how people move forward together.
Schools are not places to learn a rote curriculum but to cultivate your innate gifts and tap into the intelligences of the world around you.
Education is not about testing, about learning.
Families have time to educate their kids and youth
Original of Translation: Las familias tienen tiempo de educar a sus niñes/jóvenes.

Content: Creative centers for everyone
People are trained in communing with the forest, gathering and preparing plant medicines.
As soon as someone bites into the apple, they know. Students are learning this and are also shaping the knowing about what they are experiencing in the world.
When I imagine the education system, I see kids not only gathered under trees with a variety of teachers–but they would be listening to and with the trees.
Kids education would include learning about what lights you up, what brings joy, how to connect with that always.

Knowledge is passed on by anyone who feels connected to a story to share. Storykeepers are in every community, listening and asking. Sitting on stoops in cities, talking to young children sharing their imagined stories of what will be; to leaders sharing what has been. Storykeepers visit elders considering embarking on their journeys to ancestral realms to plan their knowledge, their ike transfers. These are processes of naming the stories to be told, where they have documented them already, and who should keep the flame after them. People freely share how to do things in apprentice circles that you can find all over - in person instead of on YouTube.  You can find a group of knitters, coders, or architects who are willing to talk about how they came to know what they know and share enough to get the curious going along their paths. Knowledge is held in the commons, in the University of Life. In the Community of Knowers.

Education is a right but we no longer depend on the system of k-12 and college that has been built. Everyone can design their own path. Community based schools teach reading, writing, science, arithmetics. But we live in a world where farmers, woodworkers, plumbers, artists, child care workers, teachers, caretakers are seen with as much respect and with as much compensation as we give Doctors, lawyers, engineers…

Schools have been transformed to be ways to nurture community good, community needs, community desires. Schools are ways young people learn  stewardship of community. High school academies are places young people learn about stewardship of the environment, children’s development, health care, mental health & thriving. Student and young people led projects are the norm.  Teachers jobs are some of the best paid jobs in the country (well, there’s a guaranteed annual income that is so high that people can work in whatever fields that they want!)

People feel safe, and their purpose evolves throughout life.  Starting at about age 16, young people start choosing specialized multigenerational educational and apprenticeship groups anchored by elders that teach practices and skills related to their purpose.

Education is a progression through life. We understand ourselves as teachers early on in our lives and by 11 or 12 we take on educating those coming up behind us. We have spaces for meditation and spaces to work through anger and other big feelings – for expression in healthy, fun, rageful ways.
Collective knowledge is produced, and knowledge is shared with the collective.

They knew they could keep learning whatever they wanted to learn, and that they could share it with others.  They knew about different kinds of foods and languages, they knew different histories, and they knew that it was okay to dream their own dreams of learning and contributing.
And education is being around other people.  It is not in a classroom, a container.  It's out in the environment, up in a tree, and on the ground, and it's not in a container.
The quality of infrastructure is the same in all neighborhoods. Quality education can happen in any school, where the student body is integrated.

There is no formal education as it used to be. There is oral story telling. Ancestor connection. We have reclaimed knowledge because we know longer rely on the systems. The apocalypse allowed us to leapfrog into freedom, and we had to let it go.
Learning happens in all directions – from younger to elder and vice versa– through…
Learning happens through song, dance, storytelling, and all forms of art, beauty and  pleasure.
Learning takes place beyond a classroom—that teachers are guides and stewards imagining the future guides and stewards of this place.
Community teachers and mentors is the norm

Children’s books are culturally relevant to their lives; books are returned more in studies than digital tech; education has cultural teaching components; cultural responsiveness in woven withing all of society; school-community collaborative responsiveness models. Families and dogs are playing and walking in the park.
Education is free and there are multiple ways of learning.  No one way of learning is more important than the other.  All skills are needed  and valued in community.
Mocking no longer happens.  Education is designed to support healing in tapping into all paths, and sickness is tended to before folks are sick.
Custom educational systems.
There are elders holding conversations on each corner that are master classes in life–and all things important to living a happy and joyful life.

Social and emotional education is taught in every school, work and social setting. Everyone knows how to share their feelings and feel their feelings. We embrace all our feelings and each other's feelings. We know how to resolve conflict through no-violent communication. This is an ability passed down by parents, grandparents, and close relatives. Schools and work settings affirm these ways of being by teaching and structuring their practices around these teachings.
All pathways to knowledge are celebrated and pursued
Embodied knowledge is seen to be as valuable, as learned knowledge & children are taught to listen to what their bodies have to say from an earlier age

Peer pressure has been transformed into peer compassion and empathy. Middle school students love going to school throughout puberty. They feel comfortable in their bodies with their braces, pimples and hormonal changes.
Learning is always happening, everyone teaches everyone, a teacher means sharing knowledge no matter what age or place in society
There’s a school to neighborhood roles process, so learners get to apply their skills in their neighborhoods with their people
A 5 year old kid being picked up from school has healthy food.  His education is great, and he gets picked up by his grandparents.

There is a student body.  There is a new person stepping into the school not knowing anyone…but everyone else knows one another.  They have some challenges, but don’t say anything about it.  The challenges start to break them down until they talk about it.  The people around them start sharing ways they have struggled in the same ways…and this new student doesn’t feel so alone anymore.  They all discover a common goal to problem solve around together.

Many forms of wisdom are respected. Knowledge flows not just in one direction and not just from one source. When I am curious about how things are made in Japan, I go there to learn directly from the people there.

Date/Circle Name: 2/27/25 Redwood City and North Fair Oaks, CA Sobrato 2
Content: There is compassion for others, building things with our hands, connection to other communities are a central part of education and shared learning for young people.

Date/Circle Name: 3/11/25 Community Change Women of Color retreat
Content: Education is free and innovation is at the core of our society.

Date/Circle Name: 3/11/25 Community Change Women of Color retreat
Content: Teachers and healers are the most respected roles in our society.

Date/Circle Name: 3/11/25 Community Change Women of Color retreat
Content: We practice deep listening in our conversations.

Content: We have the ability to communicate in every language.

Math classrooms have lots of windows.  Multiple languages flow in and out of use, and everyone understands.  There are holograms that immediately show 3d models of things being taught.  Kids don’t talk about recess anymore, because they choose into classrooms and truly enjoy their time.
Kids learn that 1 + 1 = 2 in some circumstances – like building a building in relationship to the landscape…and that 1+1=11 and 1 +1+1 = 111 when it comes to relationships and critical mass.
Schools…there is math, history etc. but schools have a lot more storytelling and learning through doing.  Teachers pay close attention to what kids love and are good at–and nourish it.
Schools are adaptable…lots of kids learn practical skills.
Wisdom and knowledge are cultivated freely.  We have many ways of teaching one another to be in the rhythm of life.

The standard of education will be that there is more space for children to grow and choose what they are going to do. Countries will collaborate more instead of setting borders. Children will understand how to collaborate with nature and grow up in community to serve each other instead of fighting for limited resources.
Knowledge is story-based. There is no longer such a focus on testing and performance.  There is a communal sense of learning from one another.
Open access to collective knowledge.
free education and free health care for everyone.
data doesn’t move faster than knowledge doesn’t move faster than wisdom
education is a generational transfer, and reciprocal

We learn to thrive. We learn with the purpose of thriving. We share stories orally and in written form. We value questions, how and why, and we value questioning. Learning will be rooted in the places that we are. In the soil. Treasuring the art. Learning history of place for what is and what is to come. There are spaces to learn how to read, write, and the languages of numbers. Learning happens with high support and high expectations, but not about individual performance, but for each other. Holding the north star collectively. Generative conflict. Generative connection.
Education has a different focus, really develops kids talents and we educate our kids to do what they love while serving the community.

Multi-generational schools exist in close relationship with care giving centers for healing, older people, attending to people’s mental health.  These schools and centers, in close relationship, make everyone feel safer.

We exist in an environment where we meet each other fully.  We are in right relationship.  We have regard for each other.  When we meet, our hearts are always listening and saying “tell me more.”  This respectful way of being in relationship has been normalized since we stopped being interested in dominance in relationships.

Our schools no longer test but nurture. Children grow gardens, learn by story, and discover their gifts without pressure. They dream of being artists, farmers, healers, valued for how they serve their communities, not for how much they earn.

In 2025 information was the rage, even as knowledge was tossed to the Wayside. 
In 2025 facts were discounted. There was no patience for facts.  

Now, we remember the value of common sense folk. We know the importance of listening to elders, voices trembling. We hear inconvenient voices. We face the facts.

In our shared horizon, we know there is much we do not know, and some things we’ll never know. We know that cycles of inquiry serve our desire for knowledge. 

We also know that discovering an answer is not a final destination or solution. We know that some answers can have binary impacts, seen and unseen, on our peoples and our world. 

We offer spaces and ways to practice connection and attention. Context matters. 

Ideas blow around - life is our own and belongs as a thread within a larger three-dimensional web of space and time. 

We recognize that balance contains counterbalance. We understand that what seems good for the wolf may or may not be good for the sheep. 

We know the definition of limits are much more vast than our own.

We learned from the school movements and experiments that came before us and that we survived. 

Education is a lifelong verb, not something done to others. Justice and peace are integrative, not afterthoughts. Apprenticeships are a valuable way we grow.

Children's voices are respected and valued and shared.

We seek to guide and facilitate more than we teach. We stoke curiosity and complexity and critical thinking and credibility of sources. We look to ignite passion and love for belonging, community and purpose.

Children and teachers problem solve together. 

Children once again grow up in a village where they learn from aunties and Grandma's and cousins.
Intuition is favored over data. Information is 100% at everyone's fingertips so that knowledge and creativity grow.

Learning happens in circles, adults, children and elders. History is taught through love and compassion. We recount the stories of how we have loved and harmed each other but finally understood what it took to heal.

Learning happens in trees, intergenerational. History is always taught – starting with how we feel in relationship with each other and how we've loved and harmed over the centuries and what it took to heal.
Education is not a place, it is a way of learning. No power, no hate. We share with one another.
We value learning about how to best care and love each other.
In education there will be traditional and non-traditional forms honored.  Both formal and informal education will have resources and funding.
Having culturally-relevant curriculum that is taught in our fully-funded and resourced schools that is taught from different perspectives and not of the colonizers.
Education is set up for curiosity and learning skills
All people are welcome to learn and explore new skills and interests to add value to community learning and mentor others.

One way keiki are honored is through their education. Keiki learn from many adults and from each other. All knowledge is not taught in the same school – and each educational experience is hyper-personalized. Knowledge held in the body and in the hands is valued as much in education as knowledge held in the mind. Keiki are able to take the knowledge stored in their minds, bodies, and hands with them wherever they go, always prepared to surf the dynamic (sometimes chaotic) systems they encounter.
Education travels and is shared

The impulse of your education being led by what's inside you- for example by plants ppl are attracted to. That's what I’d like to see for the children- a child joyfully sharing a dream they had with classmates and grandparents. Children being able to share inner life, appreciation of the commons so much so that the commons come back, we’re all taken care of and in the hands of everyone.

In our future, children learn in all kinds of ways.

When kids are waking up to go to school in the morning, they don’t dread being stuck in a classroom all day learning about things that won’t apply to their lives. Instead, they are excited to go to an indoor-outdoor learning space where the kids are basking in the sun, surrounded by trees. Older teens collaborate with the adults to help facilitate teaching younger kids.

Learning is not about “getting ahead”.   We learn to appreciate the world and those around us by spending time in nature, working together to figure things out, and listening to each other.  We work hard at learning and we balance this with resting and napping when we need to.

What do YOU see in the schools in this future world?
Educational centers are open to everyone, with no class distinctions, and offer preparation in areas like economics, finance, and psychology.
Community schools with abundant education. Healthy food from chemical-free crops.
Free studies for all groups and universities, accessible to everyone.
Learning and teaching are embraced by everyone and seen as being the responsibility of everyone – not relegated to certain times in your life or certain roles.
All education would be free, including musical education, agriculture, medicine, engineering, law and history

Places of learning both in the community with more home-based and experiential opportunities.  Spaces for more extensive education for specialties, e.g. healing others, that people can easily get to by air in a short time.
Curriculum allows for discovery of gifts and talents. Love is the common yardstick for everything.

There is a trades person with a blue hammer and a house. Children are inside the windows with joyful smiles on their faces.  They are learning to create with their hands. They have learned through mentorship, kindness and patience.
School is the central community center where we learn from our ancestors. Open access areas for connecting to other people.
Mentorship thrives as a primary way to pass on knowledge and skills.

Information is abundant, and students of all ages are engaged. The learning environment is diverse safe and open, with equal contribution from tech and traditional. “What are you learning today?” is the asked regularly.
One thing that does exist is meaningful learning. We cultivate curiosity and compassion. We nurture each other. We aim to live meaningful lives.

Education is very locally based. Elders who have knowledge share their learning. Teachers are seen as wisdom keepers. They have autonomy over how best to meet the needs of students in their care. Classroom days and times are flexible and flow in relationship to the community.

Young people don’t go hungry. We learn from the land. There is quality instruction in reading and writing and art and science. There is holistic sex education. Educators are supported by families and the community. There is co-ownership of learning and the places called school.
In fact - schools are sanctuaries. Places of belonging with attention to each student. And they are places where students build their confidence and skills.
The time when schools seemed like boxed prisons and where there was a militarized culture and actual threats for who comes to school are far in the past.
Learning is hands-on and interactive. We learn about permaculture, relationality, and how to pursue our interests and ways to support each other.
There's not one way to learn - that makes no sense.
And we have fantastic outdoors spaces along with larger library and learning spaces with comfortable chairs and REAL books!

Generativity and helping the younger generation is a shared goal in society. People of all ages are recognized as having value and knowledge. People who are accomplished in their fields and others who
want to learn similar things come together locally and from afar to help these dreams come
true. Learning doesn’t stop at a certain age but learning experiences are available to all
ages without going into debt to obtain it.
Education is done cohort or community style.  You build connections and relationships in education … because you don’t need to build knowledge due to technology.
Everyone will have access to everything…but teachers will still help people with their struggles to develop and evolve.

Kids are taught human connection practices and skills in schools, and we learn ways to manage conflicts and find ways to resolve differences. Kids are outside, learning from the plants and trees and water. We have developed new ways of building character and resilience.

Children play and learn unencumbered by fear (school shooting; sectarian violence) or food insecurity anxiety on their own schedule. Educational systems have slack and capacity to absorb humans that need to be prioritized. New parents are supported by the community & do not have to focus on anything other than their family.

Kids love going to school . . . two hours are spent learning in ways that are personalized to their learning style, their interests, and their abilities . . . but the rest of school time is spent creating. A key goal of education is to discover one’s sense of purpose in relationship to community.

Date/Circle Name: 10/29/25 Kailua, HI Kahanaiki Group, Le Jardin Academy
Content: We’ve learned from working with the keiki. We hunt boar. We work down at Kahanaiki, Palalupe, and with Pōhaku. The teachers have taught the younger generation to bring the land back.

Date/Circle Name: 10/30/25 Kailua, HI Kipuka Pala'a Group, Le Jardin Academy
Content: Every month we visit the school’s wetland marsh to work with the wild kids club. We plant and care for the native species and canoe plants that have all come back: ti leaves, kukui, koa, native hibiscus, kalo, maiʻa. The community feeds itself from our gardens. The food waste is food for the animals. The teachers have taken on the role of the wisdom sharers. 150 years ago they planted the seed and set the intention. Teachers and students now work and learn together. Hawaiian leaders have taught us how to build and farm.

Date/Circle Name: 10/30/25 Kailua, HI Polynesian Club, Le Jardin Academy
Content: Teachers and biologists share stories and knowledge of how this place used to be, so we remember and not repeat.

Date/Circle Name: 10/30/25 Kailua, HI Polynesian Club, Le Jardin Academy
Content: Every week schools meet on the coast, in the mountains, or at the beach to start with an hour of clean up.
Education and knowledge in relationship with nature
Education - land and natural world is teaching element shoreline is classroom
Central value of our educational systems focus on child rearing towards responsibility for one another and all beings
Archival knowledge not gate kept by university
The whole person is developed and supported in a way where silence is the teacher.

Learning is engaging.  It’s an intimate expression of acknowledging choices, consequences and practicing being in relationship with people, plans, environments, animals, community or systems different than your own with openness, curiosity and cultivating abundance.

We will learn from each other –  how to organize the masses and build a sustainable movement. I see us more educated, not just school wise but also culturally, agriculturally, and world-widely.  I hope to see the school system not corrupted and free schooling/education. Education is free for life and everyone is encouraged to be forever learners. Holders of wisdom aren’t limited by age or status. Curiosity and wonder, experimentation and learning are core values in how we communally navigate the world and our relationships to one another.
In schools we receive wisdom.

Children are smiling and eager to come to school while teachers of all different backgrounds welcome them in. Classrooms are engaging and conversations are inquisitive and meaningful. Schools are a place of love, learning, community and intentional growth.
Parents and families are involved in education. We look to the past and spend time understanding history and bringing forward essential wisdom and knowledge.
Learning happens with Lola, Lolos, Titas, Titos, during mahjong.

The ability to enjoy life without worrying about tomorrow. Basic education skills like reading and addition / subtraction will be taught in every household, while schools focus on specific career and financial literacy.

Como es que la educación se hace? Ensenar cosas del pasado que se han perdidos gracias la tecnologia. How is education conducted? By teaching things from the past that have been lost due to technology.

Nowadays, our schools are taught with the land and elders, outside as much as possible. Education is an exploration informed by broad and deep cultural knowledge. It values intuitive knowledge and allows for “failure” and discomfort to transform into improvement. It is experiential, where the ocean, rivers, forests, deserts, community gardens are the classrooms as well as the homes.

Community schools are integrated into local clusters and neighborhoods. Life skills classes (cooking, cleaning, financial literacy, communication and handling conflict) are taught in all schools from a young age and support youth to find opportunities to stay local after college to help improve their communities. Education is open to anyone who wants to learn, without any restrictions like money, country or gender.
And we teach what we know through practices passed down by our parents.
Original of Translation: Y enseñamos lo que sabemos con prácticas que nos enseñaron nuestros padres.

Content: May all humans in the world, and especially girls, have the right to education.
Original of Translation: Que todos los humanos del mundo y especialmente las niñas tengan el derecho a la educación.

Content: Accessible, high quality education for everyone

School grounds filled with grass/nature, trees, vegetation, small animals, children in small group circles with many teachers that are engaged, experimenting, hands on learning, fresh air, buildings that are not concrete/steel, singing songs, diverse languages and cultures being welcomed and children affirmed and proud of their heritage, where families are welcomed in, invited and they can join without worrying about needing to go to their jobs.
The process of learning…new themes, language, and willingness to get out of our comfort zone. A community of understanding, safety, and love.
